stem: An adult is admitted to a hospital unit because of a primary behavioral health condition. Which nursing action best reflects current Joint Commission suicide-risk standards?

options.A: Screen the client for suicidal ideation using a validated screening tool and follow an evidence-based assessment process if the screen is positive.
options.B: Skip suicide screening unless the client spontaneously states an intent to die.
options.C: Use an informal conversation only, because validated tools are not required when behavioral health is the primary reason for care.
options.D: Assume that universal suicide-risk screening is required for every hospital patient regardless of the reason for care.

rationale: A is correct. The Joint Commission’s current suicide-risk performance goal requires screening patients being evaluated or treated primarily for a behavioral health condition for suicidal ideation using a validated screening tool and using an evidence-based process for further assessment when indicated. B is incorrect because the standard does not require waiting for spontaneous disclosure. C is incorrect because a validated screening tool is specifically required for this population. D is incorrect because the Joint Commission does not require universal screening of all hospital patients regardless of presentation. Separately, the USPSTF has concluded that evidence is insufficient to determine the balance of benefits and harms of universal suicide-risk screening in asymptomatic adults in primary care, reinforcing the need to avoid an unsupported universal claim.
educational_objective: Use a validated suicide-risk screening tool for clients whose primary reason for care is a behavioral health condition, then complete evidence-based follow-up assessment and safety planning according to the result and clinical presentation.
source_document_title: National Performance Goal #8: Reducing the Risk for Suicide; Standards FAQ — Suicide Risk Reduction Screening Requirements
source_version_date: Current Joint Commission National Performance Goals; FAQ updated April 21, 2026; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: National Performance Goal #8 — hospitals must screen patients being treated primarily for a behavioral health condition for suicidal ideation using a validated tool and use an evidence-based process for positive screens; Standards FAQ NPSG/NPG suicide-risk screening requirements — screening is not required universally for all patients
source_claim_supported: Joint Commission standards require validated suicide-ideation screening for patients whose primary reason for care is a behavioral health condition and evidence-based follow-up assessment when indicated; the requirement is not universal for every hospital patient.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Psychosocial Integrity — recognize and respond to clients at risk for self-harm/suicide and provide a safe therapeutic environment; integrated clinical judgment and safety processes
blueprint_topic: Psychosocial Integrity — suicide-risk screening and follow-up in behavioral health care
correction_summary: The source item overgeneralized routine suicide-risk screening to general health assessments. The final item narrows the population to one explicitly covered by current Joint Commission standards, removes the unsupported universal claim, and reclassifies the item from Health Promotion and Maintenance to Psychosocial Integrity.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current Joint Commission National Performance Goal #8 and its suicide-risk screening FAQs, including an FAQ updated in April 2026. The original broad statement was contradicted by both Joint Commission scope language and the USPSTF 2023 I statement for asymptomatic adults in primary care.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: The final stem specifies the population to which the Joint Commission requirement applies. A states the validated-screen plus evidence-based follow-up sequence without inventing a particular proprietary tool or reassessment interval.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct. It directly matches current Joint Commission requirements for patients treated primarily for behavioral health conditions.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect. Screening is not contingent on spontaneous disclosure in this covered population.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect. An informal conversation alone does not satisfy the validated-tool requirement.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect. Joint Commission explicitly states that universal screening of every patient is not required.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A is consistent with the defined population and current standard. D was made plausible by common institutional universal-screening policies, but the stem asks what the Joint Commission standard itself requires.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address screening scope or method and are comparable in length; no answer depends on alarmist wording.
audit_findings.blueprint: Psychosocial Integrity is the best category because the nurse is identifying suicide risk and initiating evidence-based behavioral-health safety assessment.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited Joint Commission 2026 scope, universal-screening misconception, USPSTF adult evidence statement, validated-tool requirement, positive-screen follow-up, institutional-policy versus accreditation-standard distinction, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
